verses.zh: 兴起，发光！因为你的光已经来到！耶和华的荣耀发现照耀你。
verses.en: “Arise! Shine! For your light arrives!The splendor[NOTE:1] of the Lord shines on you!
notes: Or “glory” (so most English versions).

verses.zh: 看哪，黑暗遮盖大地，幽暗遮盖万民，耶和华却要显现照耀你；他的荣耀要现在你身上。
verses.en: For, look, darkness covers the earthand deep darkness covers[NOTE:1] the nations,but the Lord shines on you;his splendor[NOTE:2] appears over you.
notes: The verb “covers” is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
Or “glory” (so most English versions); TEV “the brightness of his presence.”

verses.zh: 万国要来就你的光；君王要来就你发现的光辉。
verses.en: Nations come to your light,kings to your bright light.

verses.zh: 你举目向四方观看；众人都聚集来到你这里。你的众子从远方而来；你的众女也被怀抱而来。
verses.en: Look all around you![NOTE:1] They all gather and come to you—your sons come from far away,and your daughters are escorted by guardians.
notes: Heb “Lift up around your eyes and see!”

verses.zh: 那时，你看见就有光荣；你心又跳动又宽畅；因为大海丰盛的货物必转来归你；列国的财宝也必来归你。
verses.en: Then you will look and smile,[NOTE:1] you will be excited and your heart will swell with pride.[NOTE:2] For the riches of distant lands[NOTE:3] will belong to you,and the wealth of nations will come to you.
notes: Or “shine,” or “be radiant” (NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV).
Heb “and it will tremble and be wide, your heart.”
Heb “the wealth of the sea,” i.e., wealth that is transported from distant lands via the sea.

verses.zh: 成群的骆驼，并米甸和以法的独峰驼必遮满你；示巴的众人都必来到；要奉上黄金乳香，又要传说耶和华的赞美。
verses.en: Camel caravans will cover your roads,[NOTE:1] young camels from Midian and Ephah.All the merchants of Sheba[NOTE:2] will come,bringing gold and incenseand singing praises to the Lord.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “an abundance of camels will cover you.”
Heb “all of them, from Sheba.”
Heb “and they will announce the praises of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 基达的羊群都必聚集到你这里，尼拜约的公羊要供你使用，在我坛上必蒙悦纳；我必荣耀我荣耀的殿。
verses.en: All the sheep of Kedar will be gathered to you;the rams of Nebaioth will be available to you as sacrifices.[NOTE:1] They will go up on my altar acceptably,[NOTE:2] and I will bestow honor on my majestic temple.
notes: Heb “will serve you,” i.e., be available as sacrifices (see the next line). Another option is to understood these “rams” as symbolic of leaders who will be subject to the people of Zion. See v. 10.

Heb “they will go up on acceptance [on] my altar.” Some have suggested that the preposition עַל (ʿal) is dittographic (note the preceding יַעֲלוּ [yaʿalu]). Consequently, the form should be emended to לְרָצוֹן (leratson, “acceptably”; see BDB 953 s.v. רָצוֹן). However, the Qumran scroll 1QIsaa has both לרצון followed by the preposition על, which would argue against deleting the preposition. As the above translation seeks to demonstrate, the preposition עַל (ʿal) indicates a norm (“in accordance with acceptance” or “acceptably”; IBHS 218 §11.2.13e, n. 111), and the “altar” functions as an objective accusative with a verb of motion (cf. Gen 49:4; Lev 2:2; Num 13:17; J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah [NICOT], 2:534, n. 14).

verses.zh: 那些飞来如云、又如鸽子向窗户飞回的是谁呢？
verses.en: Who are these who float along[NOTE:1] like a cloud,who fly like doves to their shelters?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “fly” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV); NAB, NIV “fly along.”
Heb “to their windows,” i.e., to the openings in their coops. See HALOT 83 s.v. אֲרֻבָּה.

verses.zh: 众海岛必等候我，首先是他施的船只，将你的众子连他们的金银从远方一同带来，都为耶和华―你　神的名，又为以色列的圣者，因为他已经荣耀了你。
verses.en: Indeed, the coastlands[NOTE:1] look eagerly for me;the large ships[NOTE:2] are in the lead,bringing your sons from far away,along with their silver and gold,to honor the Lord your God,[NOTE:3] the Holy One of Israel,[NOTE:4] for he has bestowed honor on you.
notes: Or “islands” (NIV); CEV “distant islands”; TEV “distant lands.”
Heb “the ships of Tarshish.” See the note at 2:16.
Heb “to the name of the Lord your God.”
See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

verses.zh: 外邦人必建筑你的城墙；他们的王必服事你。我曾发怒击打你，现今却施恩怜恤你。
verses.en: Foreigners will rebuild your walls;their kings will serve you.Even though I struck you down in my anger,I will restore my favor and have compassion on you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in my favor I will have compassion on you.”

verses.zh: 你的城门必时常开放，昼夜不关；使人把列国的财物带来归你，并将他们的君王牵引而来。
verses.en: Your gates will remain open at all times;they will not be shut during the day or at nightso that the wealth of nations may be delivered,with their kings leading the way.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “led in procession.” The participle is passive.

verses.zh: 哪一邦哪一国不事奉你，就必灭亡，也必全然荒废。
verses.en: Indeed,[NOTE:1] nations or kingdoms that do not serve you will perish;such nations will definitely be destroyed.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “For” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); TEV “But.”
The infinitive absolute appears before the finite verb for emphasis.

verses.zh: 黎巴嫩的荣耀，就是松树、杉树、黄杨树，都必一同归你，为要修饰我圣所之地；我也要使我脚踏之处得荣耀。
verses.en: The splendor of Lebanon will come to you, its evergreens, firs, and cypresses together,to beautify my palace;[NOTE:1] I will bestow honor on my throne room.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “holy place, sanctuary.”
Heb “the place of my feet.” See Ezek 43:7, where the Lord’s throne is called the “place of the soles of my feet.”

verses.zh: 素来苦待你的，他的子孙都必屈身来就你；藐视你的，都要在你脚下跪拜。他们要称你为「耶和华的城」，为「以色列圣者的锡安」。
verses.en: The children of your oppressors will come bowing to you;all who treated you with disrespect will bow down at your feet.They will call you, ‘The City of the Lord,Zion of the Holy One of Israel.’[NOTE:1]
notes: See the note on the phrase “the Holy One of Israel” in 1:4.

verses.zh: 你虽然被撇弃被厌恶，甚至无人经过，我却使你变为永远的荣华，成为累代的喜乐。
verses.en: You were once abandoned and despised, with no one passing through,but I will make you[NOTE:1] a permanent source of prideand joy to coming generations.
notes: Heb “Instead of your being abandoned and despised, with no one passing through, I will make you.”

verses.zh: 你也必吃万国的奶，又吃君王的奶。你便知道我―耶和华是你的救主，是你的救赎主，雅各的大能者。
verses.en: You will drink the milk of nations;you will nurse at the breasts of kings.[NOTE:1] Then you will recognize that I, the Lord, am your Deliverer,your Protector,[NOTE:2] the Powerful One of Jacob.[NOTE:3]
notes: The nations and kings are depicted as a mother nursing her children. Restored Zion will be nourished by them as she receives their wealth as tribute.
Or “redeemer.” See the note at 41:14.

verses.zh: 我要拿金子代替铜，拿银子代替铁，拿铜代替木头，拿铁代替石头；并要以和平为你的官长，以公义为你的监督。
verses.en: Instead of bronze, I will bring you gold;instead of iron, I will bring you silver;instead of wood, I will bring you[NOTE:1] bronze;instead of stones, I will bring you[NOTE:2] iron.I will make prosperity[NOTE:3] your overseer,and vindication your sovereign ruler.[NOTE:4]
notes: The words “I will bring you” are supplied in the translation; they are understood by ellipsis (see the preceding lines).
The words “I will bring you” are supplied in the translation; they are understood by ellipsis (see the first two lines of the verse).
Or “peace” (KJV and many other English versions).

The plural indicates degree. The language is ironic; in the past Zion was ruled by oppressive tyrants, but now personified prosperity and vindication will be the only things that will “dominate” the city.

verses.zh: 你地上不再听见强暴的事，境内不再听见荒凉毁灭的事。你必称你的墙为「拯救」，称你的门为「赞美」。
verses.en: Sounds of violence will no longer be heard in your land,or the sounds of[NOTE:1] destruction and devastation within your borders.You will name your walls, ‘Deliverance’and your gates, ‘Praise.’
notes: The words “sounds of” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 日头不再作你白昼的光；月亮也不再发光照耀你。耶和华却要作你永远的光；你　神要为你的荣耀。
verses.en: The sun will no longer supply light for you by day,nor will the moon’s brightness shine on you;the Lord will be your permanent source of light—the splendor of your God will shine upon you.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and your God for your splendor.”

verses.zh: 你的日头不再下落；你的月亮也不退缩；因为耶和华必作你永远的光。你悲哀的日子也完毕了。
verses.en: Your sun will no longer set;your moon will not disappear;[NOTE:1] the Lord will be your permanent source of light;your time[NOTE:2] of sorrow will be over.
notes: In this verse “sun” and “moon” refer to the Lord’s light, which will replace the sun and moon (see v. 19). Light here symbolizes the restoration of divine blessing and prosperity in conjunction with the Lord’s presence. See 30:26.
Heb “days” (so KJV, NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT).

verses.zh: 你的居民都成为义人，永远得地为业；是我种的栽子，我手的工作，使我得荣耀。
verses.en: All your people will be godly;[NOTE:1] they will possess the land permanently.I will plant them like a shoot;they will be the product of my labor,through whom I reveal my splendor.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “righteous” (NASB, NIV, NRSV, NLT); NAB “just.”
Heb “a shoot of his planting, the work of my hands, to reveal splendor.”

verses.zh: 至小的族要加增千倍；微弱的国必成为强盛。我―耶和华要按定期速成这事。
verses.en: The least of you will multiply into[NOTE:1] a thousand;the smallest of you will become a large nation.When the right time comes, I the Lord will quickly do this!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “will become” (so NASB, NIV).
Heb “I, the Lord, in its time, I will quickly do it.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- There is a radical change in the mood between Isaiah 59 and Isaiah 60-62.

- Isaiah 60-62 form a unit that deals with the glorious future of God's people as depicted
in the restoration of Jerusalem.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 60:1-3

1"Arise, shine; for your light has come,

And the glory of the Lord has risen upon you.

2For behold, darkness will cover the earth

And deep darkness the peoples;

But the Lord will rise upon you

And His glory will appear upon you.

3Nations will come to your light,

And kings to the brightness of your rising.

60:1 "Arise, shine" Two Qal IMPERATIVES implore the covenant people to
be what they were called to be for themselves and for the world (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN).

Light is recurrent imagery in this chapter to describe:

- God's presence, Isa. 60:1,2,9-20; Rev. 21:23; 22:5

- spiritual holiness, Isa. 60:1,3,5,21; 62:1

- recurring imagery of light in Isaiah (cf. Isa. 9:2; 42:6; 49:6; 58:8; 59:9)

SPECIAL TOPIC: LIGHT

▣ "your light has come" The subject of Isa. 60:1-22 is "Zion" (cf. Isa. 60:14), which symbolizes the people of God.

The common VERB "come" (BDB 97, KB 112) is used several times in this chapter.

- has come ‒ Qal PERFECT, Isa. 60:1

- come ‒ Qal PERFECT, Isa. 60:4

- will come ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:4

- will come ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:5

- will come ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:6

- will bring ‒ Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, Isa. 60:6

- bring ‒ same as #6, Isa. 60:11

- will come ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:13

- will bring ‒ Hiphil IMPERFECT, twice, Isa. 60:17

- same as #9

- will set ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, Isa. 60:20

Remember the time element is not in the Hebrew VERB but in its use in context.

▣ "the glory of the Lord" This is parallel to "light" in line 1. It is
used in other places in Isaiah connected to light/lights (cf. Isa. 24:23; 58:8) and agricultural abundance
(cf. Isa. 35:2). The Hebrew term for "glory" (BDB 458), because of its association with the Shekinah
cloud of glory (cf. Exod. 13:21-22; 14:19,20,24; 19:16-18; 20:21), symbolized YHWH's personal presence with
the Israelites during the Exodus. Fire and lightning were associated with the coming of YHWH to Mt. Sinai
(cf. Exodus 19-20), so brightness became an aspect of "glory."

Notice YHWH's glory.

- will rise ‒ BDB 280, KB 281, Qal IMPERFECT

- will appear ‒ BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT

SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH

SPECIAL TOPIC: GLORY (OT)

60:2 This has some allusion to the physical darkness of Gen. 1:1-2 or Exod. 10:21-23 or even Isa. 9:2,
and the spiritual darkness caused by sin. YHWH will not allow the darkness of the Fall (cf. Genesis 3), which
covers all humans, to remain. His "light" of revelation and salvation will rise (Qal IMPERFECT,
BDB 280, KB 281).

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

SPECIAL TOPIC: DARKNESS

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "earth" Erets (BDB 75, KB 90) has a wide semantic field.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAND, COUNTRY, EARTH

60:3 "Nations will come to your light" It is obvious that God's original purpose for Israel was to bring
the world to Himself (cf. Isa. 61:6,11b; 62:2,11; Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5-6).

Of all the prophets, with the possible exceptions of Micah and Jonah, it is Isaiah who saw the universal implications of

- monotheism (see SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM)

- OT Patriarchal promises (see SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS)

- Israel's evangelistic purpose (see SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN)

Note Isa. 2:2-4; 12:4-5; 42:6-12; 45:14,22-25; 49:23; 51:4-5; 56:6-7; 60:1-3; 66:23. This is surely
the precursor of John 3:16; 4:42; 1 Tim. 2:4; Titus 2:11; 2 Pet. 3:9; I John 2:2; 4:14. The NT, following the
teachings of Jesus, universalized the OT promises to Israel (cf. Gen. 12:3; Exod. 19:5), to the whole world
(cf. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:47; Acts 1:8). Neither Jesus nor any NT Apostle ever reaffirms a national promise to Israel.
The OT has been fulfilled and overflowed in the Gospel (cf. Matt. 5:17-19; Eph. 2:11-3:13).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 60:4-9

4"Lift up your eyes round about and see;

They all gather together, they come to you.

Your sons will come from afar,

And your daughters will be carried in the arms.

5Then you will see and be radiant,

And your heart will thrill and rejoice;

Because the abundance of the sea will be turned to you,

The wealth of the nations will come to you.

6A multitude of camels will cover you,

The young camels of Midian and Ephah;

All those from Sheba will come;

They will bring gold and frankincense,

And will bear good news of the praises of the Lord.

7All the flocks of Kedar will be gathered together to you,

The rams of Nebaioth will minister to you;

They will go up with acceptance on My altar,

And I shall glorify My glorious house.

8Who are these who fly like a cloud

And like the doves to their lattices?

9Surely the coastlands will wait for Me;

And the ships of Tarshish will come first,

To bring your sons from afar,

Their silver and their gold with them,

For the name of the Lord your God,

And for the Holy One of Israel because He has glorified you.

60:4 "Lift up. . .see" These are two Qal IMPERATIVES (cf. Isa. 49:18; John 4:35).
In this section of Isaiah IMPERATIVES often begin a new strophe.

▣ "Your sons will come from afar" In Isaiah 60-62, there are two major eschatological signs that deal with traveling.

- the people of God will return to their ancestral home, symbolized by the city of Jerusalem

- the nations, instead of taking the Jews prisoner and deporting them, will come to the people of God with gifts and praise

60:5 As a result of God's repentant people "seeing" (Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 906, KB 1157),
notice the stated consequences of seeing the light of God (cf. Isa. 60:1,4,19,20).

- be radiant ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw, BDB 626, KB 676

- thrill (lit. tremble) ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw, BDB 808, KB 922

- rejoice ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw, BDB 931, KB 1210

The reasons for this hope and joy are God's gracious acts.

- the abundance of the seas will be turned to you (i.e. the wealth of the seafaring peoples)

- the wealth of the nations will come to you (cf. Isa. 60:6-7,11; 61:6)

These parallel lines of poetry describe the gratitude of the nations for Israel's

- revealing of YHWH

- bringing the reality of YHWH's presence to earth

- opening a way for their inclusion to God's covenant family (cf. Isa. 56:7)

In some ways, this parallels what happened when Israel left Egypt. Egyptians gave them gifts (cf. Exod. 12:35-36).

60:5b

NASB, NRSV, Peshitta
"rejoice"

NKJV, TEV
"with joy"

NJB
"dilate"

REB
"with gladness"

JPSOA
"thrill"

The MT has two paralleled Qal PERFECT VERBS.

- BDB 808, KB 922, "in awe"

- BDB 931, KB 931, "to be wide" or "large"

The second one is a Hebrew idiom. It referred to the excitement of a calf released from
a pen into a wide, green pasture. The joy can be expressed by a similar Hebrew root (BDB 923), but the
UBS Text Project, p. 153, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt). However, the meaning of
the line of poetry is the same.

60:6 "will bear good news of the praises of the Lord" The VERB
(Piel IMPERFECT, BDB 142, KB 163) refers to the grace of God to Israel and to all nations
(cf. Isa. 40:9-10; 41:27; 42:10-13; 52:7). Isn't it shocking to hear of the pagan nations praising the God of Israel?
This is the obvious theological goal of monotheism. There is one God and all humans are created in His image
and likeness (cf. Gen. 1:26-27) for fellowship (implication of Gen. 3:8; Lev. 26:12). The promise of Gen. 3:15 to
all humans and the hope of covenant blessings to the families of the earth in Gen. 12:3 have come to fruition.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

60:7 "Nabaioth" This refers to Arabian tribes, as the phrase, "the flocks of Kedar," does. This tribe
is mentioned in Gen. 25:13. They are called the Nabateans by the Greeks and Romans.

▣ The last two poetic lines seem to imply Gentiles acting as priests at YHWH's altar. Wow!
What a new day of inclusion (possibly linked to Isa. 56:7; 61:6-7; 66:21; 1 Pet. 2:5,9; Rev. 1:6; 5:10; 20:6).

60:8 This refers to sails of ships on the horizon coming (i.e. v. 9) to the restored and renewed Jerusalem (cf. v. 7c, d).

60:9 "Surely the coastlands will wait for Me" The term "coastlands" (or "islands," BDB 15 I) is used in this
section of Isaiah as a metaphor for all Gentiles.

The VERB "wait" (Piel IMPERFECT, BDB 875, KB 1082)
is often used of trusting in YHWH (cf. Isa. 8:17; 25:9; 26:8; 33:2). Notice how it is used of YHWH in Isa. 30:18!

▣ "the ships of Tarshish" Tarshish could refer to

- Southern Spain

- Sardinia

- a proverbial use of the ends of the earth

SPECIAL TOPIC: TARSHISH

▣ Notice the covenant names for Deity (also notice Isa. 60:14,16).

- YHWH (God as Savior and Redeemer)

- Elohim (God as creator and provider)

- Holy One of Israel (covenant God)

SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C., D.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HOLY ONE

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 60:10-14

10"Foreigners will build up your walls,

And their kings will minister to you;

For in My wrath I struck you,

And in My favor I have had compassion on you.

11Your gates will be open continually;

They will not be closed day or night,

So that men may bring to you the wealth of the nations,

With their kings led in procession.

12For the nation and the kingdom which will not serve you

will perish,

And the nations will be utterly ruined.

13The glory of Lebanon will come to you,

The juniper, the box tree and the cypress together,

To beautify the place of My sanctuary;

And I shall make the place of My feet glorious.

14The sons of those who afflicted you will come bowing

to you,

And all those who despised you will bow themselves at the

soles of your feet;

And they will call you the city of the Lord,

The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.

60:10 "For in My wrath I struck you,

And in My favor I have had compassion on you" Here we see the two major
actions of YHWH in the Bible:

- His grace (long term, cf. Ps. 103:10-14)

- His wrath (short term, cf. Isa. 57:16; Ps. 103:9)

His judgment is parental in nature and meant to cause His creation to return to Him
(cf. Romans 1-3; Heb. 12:1-13).

60:11 "Your gates will be open continually" This phrase is used to show

- security is assured

- availability is certain (cf. Rev. 21:25)

60:12 "the nation and the kingdom which will not serve you will perish" This warning is similar to
God's covenant with Abraham in Gen. 12:3.

60:13 This verse speaks of the construction of a new Holy Place (i.e. temple) with the beautiful lumber
from Lebanon (cf. 1 Kgs. 5:15-25).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TABERNACLE OF THE WILDERNESS

▣ "the place of My sanctuary;

And I shall make the place of My feet glorious" The Ark of the Covenant in
the Holy of Holies symbolizes God's presence on earth. The Jews conceived of the space between the wings

60:15-22 This passage is very similar to Rev. 21:1-27, which describes "New Jerusalem." There
have been two major opinions on the relationship of the OT promises to the NT:

- They are meant to be taken literally and Jerusalem will be rebuilt with its central sacrificial
temple, i.e. dispensational premillennialism.

- These passages are symbolic of the church and their significance is caught up in the NT
as the new people of God, i.e. amillennialism.

The same ambiguity can be seen in Isa. 61:6, where Israel is referred to as a "Priests of the
Lord" (cf. Exod. 19:6 "a Kingdom of Priests"). But these same terms are used
in 1 Pet. 2:5,9 and Rev. 1:6 to describe the church. Israel's purpose has always been to bring the world to
God (cf. Isa. 62:2,11). However, they failed and God has chosen the church to fulfill this task.
